name: Kwatl
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct Yuman variety; only classificatory discussion (Laylander 1997; Field 2012) found; no phonological description exists online.

sources.citation: Vinogradov, Igor. 2026. Ko'alh (Yuman family) case system. LIAMES 26: e026009, 1-18. doi:10.20396/liames.v26i00.8680898.
sources.note: Only in passing: p.3 'All consonant case suffixes illustrated in Table 1 have allomorphs with a short unstressed vowel, which are used with nouns ending in a consonant'; 'The locative case suffix consists of a single unstressed front vowel'; p.16 'Case markers do not participate in stress patterns.' No statement of where stress falls.

sources.citation: Langdon, Margaret. 1977. Stress, length, and pitch in Yuman languages. In L. Hyman (ed.), Studies in Stress and Accent (SCOPIL 4), 239-259. Los Angeles: USC.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Family-level only, Ko'alh/Kwatl not named (subsumed under 'Diegueno (Southern and Baja California)'): p.239 'All descriptions of Yuman languages agree that these are stress languages, and that stress is assigned morphologically to the root of the word.. regardless of the complexity of the word, the stress remains fixed on the root.'

sources.citation: Vinogradov, Igor & Manuel A. Sanchez-Fernandez (analisis), Raul Sandoval (narrador). 2025. El relato de El riano: una narracion ku'alh. Tlalocan 30(1): 253-281. doi:10.19130/iifl.tlalocan.2025.1/00XS3R100X95.
sources.note: Nothing; 'Convenciones ortograficas' (pp.263-264) covers graphemes only (lh, tx, x, sh, j, ñ, ch, apostrophe); stress not marked or discussed. Useful history of research (Owen 1960, Joel 1964, Robles Uribe 1964, INALI 2010, Field & Miller).

sources.citation: Vinogradov, Igor & Manuel Alejandro Sanchez-Fernandez. 2025. Ku'alh y kumiay: una comparacion lexica de dos lenguas yumanas. Cuadernos de Linguistica de El Colegio de Mexico 12: e340, 1-41. doi:10.24201/clecm.v12.340.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; discusses segmental correspondences Ko'alh/Kumiai (ʈ : ʈʂ, cluster simplification, lateral depalatalization citing Miller 2018:420) and gives the state of research: 'hasta la fecha no se ha publicado ningun analisis propiamente linguistico' from the Field & Miller project; notes Miller 2018 treats Mixco's ms data as a distinct variety 'kʷʔaƚʸ'.

sources.citation: INPI. 2020. Atlas de los pueblos indigenas de Mexico: Ku'ahles - Lengua.https://atlas.inpi.gob.mx/kuahles-lengua/

Field, Margaret & Amy Miller. 2018. Documentation of the Baja California Yuman Languages Kumeyaay and Ko'alh. Endangered Languages Archive, deposit dk0357. hdl:2196/00-0000-0000-000F-BF3A-4 (deposit description page).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Segmental notes only: 'Ko'alh has three contrasting sibilant phonemes', 'palatalized and non-palatalized laterals have been neutralized in Ko'alh', 'the resulting vowel system has five vowel qualities (plus a length contrast)'. Announces 'a Ko'alh grammatical sketch' (Miller in prep) not found in the archive.

sources.citation: INALI (Instituto Nacional de Lenguas Indigenas). 2010 [PDF 2012]. Proyecto de documentacion inicial de la lengua ku'ahl. Informe ejecutivo, contrato INALI.C.B.17/020/2010 (coord. M. E. Ibanez Bravo; M. Alvarado Garcia). 119 pp; annex 'Caracteristicas generales de la fonologia de la lengua ku'ahl', pp. 91-106.
sources.note: No placement rule. Plans 'elicitacion de acento.. para determinar la asignacion de acento: cabeza y direccionalidad' (p.27) and lists 'describir las caracteristicas prosodicas' as a goal (p.95) but no prosody section follows; on long vowels: 'es necesario determinar, en analisis posteriores, si el rasgo prosodico distintivo es la cantidad moraica o la intensidad' (p.98); 'cinco vocales.. porque que todas cargan acento' (p.100). Transcriptions mark stress with acute, always on the final syllable: [apá], [aʃkáʈ], [ʈaʈúc], [ʈakwák], [ʈawáy], [akáʈ], [tuʃúk] (pp.97-105); allophony rules refer to…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page kwat1246 'Kwatl' (refs: Laylander 1997; Field 2012:558).
sources.note: Nothing; classification Cochimi-Yuman > Yuman > General Yuman > Delta-Californian; AES 'extinct'; no descriptive references.

sources.citation: Miller, Amy. n.d. Guide to the writing system used in Amy Miller's transcripts of Ja'a narratives in the ELAR Archive. 2 pp. ELAR dk0357, hdl:2196/00-0000-0000-0013-108E-5.
sources.note: Ja'a Kumiai only ('Ko'alh is a different language with a different writing system. I am working on guide to the Ko'alh writing system'); mentions 'pre-stress position' allophony for Ja'a ch/sh; nothing on Ko'alh stress.
